info.name: transaction-service
info.description:
Every endpoint of transaction-service and every error it answers with, for one user, Ivan, and a second one, Anna, who must not see his data.

Nothing is copied by hand: each request stores the ids the next ones use. Run the whole collection with Postman's Runner, top to bottom. Every run makes fresh users, so it can be run again on the same databases.

Deposit and withdrawal are finished by the fake payment provider through Kafka: their status requests repeat themselves while the transaction is PENDING.

baseUrl is http://localhost:8084 - transaction-service in docker compose (make up), together with Kafka and fake-payment-provider.

exec: // a fresh user per run: the collection can be run again on the same database
pm.test('USD, ACTIVE, balance 0', () => { pm.expect(w.currencyCode).to.eql('USD'); pm.expect(w.status).to.eql('ACTIVE'); pm.expect(w.balance).to.eql(0); });
pm.test('name and type as sent', () => { pm.expect(w.name).to.eql('Main USD'); pm.expect(w.walletTypeUid).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('usdType')); });
pm.test('three wallets', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().map(w => w.name)).to.have.members(['Main USD', 'Savings USD', 'Travel EUR']));

item.name: Anna's wallets - none yet, an empty list
2. Deposit
item.description: Deposit goes through Kafka: confirm answers PENDING, the fake payment provider answers DepositCompleted or DepositFailed, the status request repeats itself until the answer is in. An amount above the provider limit (10000) is declined on purpose.

exec: pm.test('fee 0, total = amount', () => { pm.expect(t.amount).to.eql(1000); pm.expect(t.fee).to.eql(0); pm.expect(t.total).to.eql(1000); });

item.name: Deposit confirm - PENDING until the provider answers
Deposit confirm again, the same requestId - the same transaction, no second deposit
Deposit init - 20000.00, above the provider limit
Declined deposit status - wait for FAILED with the reason
Withdrawal confirm - PENDING, the reserve is taken at once
Transfer confirm - COMPLETED at once, no Kafka

exec: pm.test('both wallets, amount, fee', () => { pm.expect(t.walletUid).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('mainWallet')); pm.expect(t.targetWalletUid).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('savingsWallet')); pm.expect(t.amount).to.eql(200); pm.expect(t.fee).to.eql(1); });

item.name: Withdrawal status - for the date range below
Search without filters - all four, newest first

exec: pm.test('transfer, withdrawal, declined deposit, deposit', () => pm.expect(ids).to.eql([pm.collectionVariables.get('transferId'), pm.collectionVariables.get('withdrawalId'), pm.collectionVariables.get('declinedId'), pm.collectionVariables.get('depositId')]));
pm.test('every one a deposit', () => pm.response.json().forEach(t => pm.expect(t.type).to.eql('deposit')));

pm.test('made from Main USD: transfer, withdrawal, deposit', () => pm.expect(ids).to.eql([pm.collectionVariables.get('transferId'), pm.collectionVariables.get('withdrawalId'), pm.collectionVariables.get('depositId')]));
